transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. We have one week to get the NovaBio license package approved, so let's work through the open issues efficiently. I'd like to start by hearing from each of you in turn. Could patent, commercial, and export counsel each walk me through the key open issues you're seeing in NovaBio's current draft? I have the exclusivity, royalty rate, and sublicensing provisions flagged on my end, but I need your perspectives before I can approve the package.

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical ownership issue. While reviewing the patent ownership files this week, I confirmed that one patent essential to the licensed technology is jointly owned with Helix University. This means we cannot grant exclusivity — and the license cannot be executed — until Helix gives written consent. I have not circulated this finding beyond the patent file until now, so no one outside this room is aware of it yet. This directly impacts the exclusivity provision in NovaBio's draft and our ability to execute by next Friday.

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical export-control issue. After reviewing NovaBio's technical specifications this week, I classified the licensed encryption module as subject to U.S. export controls. This means the agreement must prohibit sublicensing to embargoed jurisdictions and require export screening before each transfer. The current draft has no export-control language whatsoever, and I have not yet marked up the draft to address this. This is directly relevant to the sublicensing provision in NovaBio's draft — we cannot permit unrestricted sublicensing without these export-control safeguards in place.
